Rwandan author, entrepreneur and cultural advocate Lisa Adeline Munezero is set to unveil her new book, “The Well of Knowing: 8 Lessons of Becoming” in Lagos State on 14 November.
In a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Saturday, Ms Munezero said the book launch will take place at Four Points by Sheraton, Victoria Island.
The book explores eight interconnected lessons on knowledge, personal growth, purposeful living and the choices that shape individual success.
According to the former Miss Rwanda contestant, the book centres on the idea that how people apply their knowledge determines the opportunities they create and the individuals they eventually become.
Ms Munezero encourages readers to rethink conventional ideas of success by examining how self-awareness, resilience, discipline and intentional actions influence the course of their lives.
She draws on her entrepreneurial journey, personal experiences and practical insights to explore these themes.

The author further explained that the book challenges readers to reflect on how they find their purpose, respond to setbacks, turn ideas into viable opportunities and use knowledge to create lasting social impact.
Through eight lessons, she explores themes such as self-awareness, accountability, resilience, entrepreneurship, continuous learning and the transfer of knowledge between generations.
Ms Munezero argued that academic qualifications, ambition, and access to opportunities do not automatically translate into fulfilment.
According to her, individuals must also show adaptability, make sound decisions, and take deliberate steps toward their goals.
“Addressing students, aspiring entrepreneurs, professionals and emerging leaders, the book presents personal development as an ongoing journey.
“It also explores mentorship, relationships and responsible leadership as ways in which individual growth can benefit communities and future generations”, said the cultural advocate and dancer.
She said she draws on her entrepreneurial experience, cultural engagement and personal reflections in her writing.
Although the book draws on African experiences, it explores universal themes of identity, ambition, adversity and opportunity.
The publication has attracted positive reviews from individuals with backgrounds in literature and professional practice.
Isi Agboaye, founder of Step Out Creatives Publications in the United Kingdom and a dramatist, praised the book for encouraging readers to identify their purpose and translate their aspirations into action.
He compared its underlying philosophy to Norman Vincent Peale’s The Power of Positive Thinking.
Meanwhile, Aderonke Adeyinka, a banking executive and author of Threads of Love and Duty, described the book as a worthwhile read for aspiring business owners and those pursuing personal development.
She noted its focus on building resilience and embracing continuous learning.
Kenyan literary journalist, blogger and podcaster James Murua also acknowledged the book’s treatment of mentorship, community connections and the preservation of knowledge through successive generations.
The gathering will allow guests to interact directly with the author and discuss the experiences and perspectives that informed the publication.
